5116.title: [skia-sync] Adopt Chrome M153 buffer upload fix
5116.body:
[skia-sync] Adopt Chrome M153 buffer upload fix (#5116)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/368
Changes: https://github.com/google/skia/compare/fca11a08da7c1ed3777b40b31611961c85c63c43...f8b66b7597c4cc859d3ed190e9c6872241e6721c

Update release/4.153.x to the actual mono/skia merge that propagates Ganesh
GPU-buffer upload failures.

Under high memory pressure, GrGpuBuffer::updateData() can fail while staging
data for a draw. Several native callers previously ignored that result and
continued as though the GPU buffer contained current data, which could allow
stale buffer contents to be drawn.

The native update propagates failures through buffer allocation and pre-draw
setup, rejects incomplete static and GL helper buffers, and drops affected
draws. Triangulated paths retain CPU-backed vertex data so a later draw can
retry GPU-buffer creation.

Pin both externals/skia and the Component Governance registration to the actual
two-parent mono/skia merge:

d457ae4d1c82de55c9a84c8957869c8617be3939

That merge contains the reviewed native commit and has the identical tree. The
upstream range changes no C API or DEPS state, so package versions, native ABI,
and the managed API remain unchanged.

5120.title: Fix BinSkim BA2007 for libHarfBuzzSharp by scoping C4244/C4267 suppression (#5111)
5120.body:
libHarfBuzzSharp.dll fails BinSkim rule BA2007 (EnableCriticalCompilerWarnings)
at error severity, because libHarfBuzzSharp.vcxproj passed
<DisableSpecificWarnings>4267;4244</DisableSpecificWarnings> in all six
ItemDefinitionGroups. C4244 and C4267 are the "possible loss of data" truncation
warnings BinSkim policy does not allow to be suppressed, so the /wd4244 /wd4267
recorded in the PDB failed the rule.

This breaks consumers, not just us: Microsoft-internal CI runs BinSkim in break
mode, and anything that takes SkiaSharp picks up HarfBuzzSharp.NativeAssets.Win32
transitively (Svg.Skia 5.x does), then fails its security gate on a binary it
does not build. The only workaround available today is to baseline it.

The project compiles exactly one translation unit -- the vendored
harfbuzz-subset.cc, itself an amalgamation of 73 upstream HarfBuzz sources -- so
there is no other object file to scope the suppression to, and BinSkim names
harfbuzz-subset.obj precisely because it is the whole binary. Building with the
suppressions removed produces 1196 warnings (976 C4244, 220 C4267), every one of
them inside vendored HarfBuzz headers and sources, so simply dropping them is not
viable and patching upstream code is not desirable.

Instead, add a small SkiaSharp-owned translation unit that wraps the vendored
amalgamation in #pragma warning(push/disable/pop) and compile that. The
suppression now lives in source rather than on the command line, so the compiler
command line recorded in the PDB is free of disabled warnings and BA2007 passes,
while any first-party code added to this project in future still gets the
warnings. libSkiaSharp is untouched -- it is clang-built and already passes.

Verified on Windows with BinSkim 4.4.9.11 (the version in the report):

  before  BA2007 error  Error_WarningsDisabled ... [Explicitly disabled warnings: 4244;4267]
  after   BA2007 pass

BA2007 now reports kind=pass on x64, ARM64 and Win32, and those are the only
results that changed -- the pre-existing BA2024/BA2025/BA2026/BA2027 warnings are
unaffected. All three platforms build with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the DLL still
exports the same 560 symbols (no ABI change), and the rebuilt binary loads and
shapes correctly (hb_version_string reports 14.2.1).

Fixes #5108

4949.title: [release] Align releases with Chromium cadence markers
4949.body:
[release] Align releases with Chromium cadence markers (#4949)

Context: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-two-week-release
Context: https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule

Align the public release train with Chromium Dash while keeping its marker
names distinct from SkiaSharp package stages. Chrome 153 starts a two-week
milestone cadence, but each train still spans about three weeks and overlaps
the next.

~~ Milestone timing ~~

Keep Preview 1 on `earliest_beta`, move Preview 2 one day earlier from
`early_stable` to `early_stable_cut`, and leave RC 1 and Stable on
`stable_cut` and `stable_date`.

For M153 onward, this places releases on days 2, 8, 15, and 22 relative to
branch point, giving gaps of 6, 7, and 7 days. Stable for one milestone and
Preview 2 for the next intentionally share a release date.

The live rollout updated Preview 2 and RC 1 metadata for M153 through M155.
A post-write dry run planned no further milestone mutations, while 4.152
reconciliation reported all 72 assignments already correct.

~~ Shared schedule vocabulary ~~

Store the Chromium Dash fields under their original names rather than the
generic `beta`, `early_stable`, and `stable` aliases. Map those fields to
SkiaSharp Preview 1, Preview 2, RC 1, and Stable only when rendering or
creating milestones.

Present Chromium markers and SkiaSharp releases in separate columns. Add a
staggered M153/M154 timeline to expose branch-relative offsets and the
overlapping release day without duplicating identical date columns.

Correct the earlier claim that Chrome moved to a three-week release cycle:
Chrome milestones now ship every two weeks, while each beta-to-stable train
continues to span about three weeks. Reject stale schedule data with an
actionable regeneration error, and pin the complete overlapping timeline and
milestone descriptions in regression tests.

4942.title: [release] Simplify workflow confirmation and split release guidance
4942.body:
[release] Simplify workflow confirmation and split release guidance (#4942)

Make remote release mutations one explicit operator decision and separate the
short shipping runbook from the implementation reference. This keeps routine
releases easy to scan without losing the invariants needed to debug or recover
the automation.

~~ Make remote writes one explicit decision ~~

Release - Prepare and Release - Finish exposed DryRun, Apply, and Push even
though Apply only changed their disposable GitHub Actions checkouts. Replace
that choice with an unchecked `push` boolean: unchecked maps to the scripts'
DryRun mode, while checked maps to Push and performs the remote writes.

Keep Apply in the PowerShell entry points because local callers retain the
prepared branches, commits, and support-file edits for inspection. Update the
release skills to teach the two-dispatch plan-then-push flow, and extend the
publishing suite to require both workflows to omit `mode`, default `push` to
false, and map it only to DryRun or Push.

~~ Separate operator steps from implementation mechanics ~~

Refocus `documentation/dev/releasing.md` as a seven-step maintainer runbook
covering the exact workflow inputs, connected Build and Tests pipelines,
optional package approval, protected publication boundary, finalization,
milestones, follow-up pull requests, and the release record.

Move the underlying sources of truth, identity transformations, HarfBuzzSharp
version coupling, signing and BAR stages, test-resource inheritance, Finish
behavior, milestone reconciliation, convergence rules, and local commands into
`documentation/dev/release-process-internals.md`.

  * Keep `-stable` as a Prepare-only confirmation sentinel so a stable cut is
    explicit. Strip it before branch creation and keep package versions, tags,
    and GitHub Releases on the bare numeric identity.

  * Mark release-testing as optional and route it through the repository skill
    with a copyable prompt. Leave the Maestro-to-NuGet.org operation as an
    explicit placeholder until its protected UI and approval sequence settle.

  * Document both accepted Finish prerelease forms. A short identity resolves
    through NuGet.org when one public build matches; zero matches stop, and an
    exact version disambiguates multiple builds.

Update the development-document index, package documentation, and release
skills to point each audience at the appropriate guide. The publishing and
milestone suites pass, and the changed documentation links resolve locally.

4933.title: Cover Push-ReleaseTag and run the release-notes tests in CI
4933.body:
Push-ReleaseTag is the irreversible step Finish uses to publish a release tag,
and it had no test coverage. A tag is immutable once a GitHub Release consumes
it, so its guards matter: refuse to act without -Push, verify the tag after
creating it, stay quiet when re-run against an identical tag, and never move a
tag that already points elsewhere. All four are now pinned, including that the
conflict is detected before -Push is considered.

Also covers the offline branches of Resolve-NuGetPackageVersion — the versions
it must return untouched rather than resolving against nuget.org. The one shape
that would reach the network is deliberately excluded, so the suite stays
deterministic. Everything drives a local bare git remote.

Separately, scripts/infra/docs/release_notes/tests holds 137 tests that nothing
ran in CI, including the GitHub Release summary mutation Finish dispatches. Adds
that step and broadens the paths filters, which matched none of
scripts/infra/docs/**, .agents/skills/release-notes/**, or
update-github-release-summaries.yml — so release-note tooling could change
without any gate running.

4930.title: Guard the docs-sync force push with an explicit lease
4930.body:
The daily docs-submodule sync pushed its PR branch with a bare `git push
--force`, which AGENTS.md forbids: a concurrent push to the same branch is
overwritten with no diagnostic.

Capture the remote tip with `git ls-remote` before `checkout -B` rewrites the
branch locally, then push with an explicit
`--force-with-lease=refs/heads/$BRANCH:$REMOTE_SHA`. A concurrent move is now
rejected with "stale info"; an empty capture is a valid lease meaning the
branch must not exist yet, so the first run still creates it.

The explicit form is used instead of a bare `--force-with-lease` because a
bare lease consults refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH, which is only present because
the checkout step sets fetch-depth: 0. At the action's default depth that ref
is absent and every push after the first is rejected, silently stalling the
sync.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

4939.title: Run the automation tooling tests in CI
4939.body:
Three test suites live in the repository, pass, and are wired to no workflow,
so a regression in any of them reaches main silently:

  .agents/skills/ci-status/scripts/tests/        8 tests
  .agents/skills/update-skia/scripts/*_test.py   4 modules
  .github/scripts/tests/skia-sync-detect.test.sh

The ci-status registry suite is the sharpest example. It exists to catch a
dashboard that reports a workflow which is not there, but nothing ran it — so
the guard itself was unguarded.

Adds a workflow covering all three, scoped tightly to the paths that feed them
plus any .github/workflows/*.yml edit, which is what makes the registry suite
re-check its tracked list whenever a workflow is added, renamed or deleted.

The ci-status suite is invoked directly rather than behind an existence check.
On the runner's Python, unittest discover already fails loudly in both
degenerate cases — exit 1 if the directory is gone, exit 5 on "NO TESTS RAN"
if it is empty — so a wrapper could only convert those into a silent pass. The
update-skia loop does need an explicit guard, because a glob that matches
nothing would otherwise iterate zero times and succeed.

Also registers the new workflow with the ci-status dashboard it runs, keeping
coverage at 27 of 29.

The registry is a hand-maintained list of workflow filenames that nothing
checked against the repository. Three defects had accumulated, none of which
surfaces as an error:

- nightly-fix-finder.lock.yml has never existed on main; it only lived on an

4920.title: [release] Automate support tier updates
4920.body:
[release] Automate support tier updates (#4920)

Make release support metadata follow published releases while retaining
maintainer control over support retirement. Standardize release automation
modes and centralize guarded file-update pull requests so local validation and
CI publishing exercise the same core path.

~~ Release-driven support membership ~~

Update scripts/infra/docs/versions.json during Release Finish, after resolving
the exact public SkiaSharp package version from NuGet. Preview and RC releases
ensure their major.minor line is present in support.preview. Stable releases
ensure the line is present in support.stable and remove that same line from
support.preview.

Retain every other stable and preview line because ending support remains an
explicit maintainer policy decision. Use PowerShell's JSON model, return the
original text when no change is needed, and preserve unrelated configuration
when updating support membership.

Document the release-driven additions and promotions while keeping removals
manual. Cover preview, RC, stable promotion, idempotency, multiple supported
lines, empty tiers, and unrelated configuration in the publishing tests.

~~ Explicit publishing modes ~~

Replace overlapping Apply and Push switches in release preparation, release
completion, and issue-template maintenance with one validated Mode parameter:
DryRun, Apply, or Push. Expose the same choices through their GitHub workflows
and release skills.

DryRun resolves and inspects the proposed state without entering the local
branch and commit path. Apply performs the same local writes, staging, branch
creation, and commit creation as Push, then stops before authentication,
remote updates, and pull-request creation. Push continues from that shared
state to publish and verify the result.

Resolve the Finish repository from the script location so invoking it by an
absolute path cannot apply changes to the caller's unrelated checkout.

~~ Guarded automation pull requests ~~

Move desired-file branch convergence into Publishing.Common and generic GitHub
pull-request creation into GitHub.Common. Reuse this path for release-support
updates and the existing bug-template version updater instead of maintaining
separate branch and PR implementations.

Require Apply and Push to start from a clean checkout at the resolved base.
Recognize an existing automation branch only when it is one commit on that
base, changes the expected paths, and contains the desired blobs. Reuse a
matching branch or open PR, replace stale owned branches with
--force-with-lease, verify the pushed SHA, and reject multiple open PRs for the
same automation branch.

The publishing suite passes 90 tests, including local Apply commits and
automation-branch reuse. The release-milestone suite passes 25 tests.

~~ Preserve HarfBuzzSharp servicing space ~~

Advance the HarfBuzzSharp package and file versions from 14.2.1.200 to
14.2.1.300 even though the native HarfBuzz revision remains 14.2.1.

Each Skia milestone reserves a 100-value package revision bucket. Reusing the
m152 .200 bucket for m153 would collide with servicing releases from the
previous milestone, so m153 starts at .300 while native dependency updates
remain independently versioned.

The versioning regression coverage passed fresh milestone, partial-run,
servicing-offset, and idempotency cases.

~~ Document reachable engine behavior ~~

Add the 4.153.0 release-note sidecar for the Linux fontconfig fallback change
that cannot appear in a managed API diff. Skia now attempts FcFontMatch before
the previous FcFontSort fallback, so applications depending on the exact
fallback face can observe different text metrics or glyphs.

Do not list the upstream Ganesh YUVA subset correction as customer-visible
SkiaSharp behavior because the affected constructors are not exposed through
the current managed or C API bindings.
